claims.text: DFT simulations can predict stable structures of noble metal–based high-entropy alloys.
DFT-predicted stable structures can enable production of NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks with precise atomic control.
A high-performance computational environment and DFT software are required for the proposed simulations.
VASP or Quantum ESPRESSO can be used to perform the proposed DFT simulations.
Templated electrodeposition or 3D printing can experimentally produce NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks after DFT structure prediction.
Combining DFT predictions with experimental fabrication can address the challenge of precise atomic control in NM-HEA nanoframeworks.
The produced NM-HEA nanoframeworks will increase catalytic efficiency by at least 20% relative to existing catalysts.
Existing catalysts have a baseline catalytic efficiency of 80 mmol/g/h.
A 20% improvement over the stated baseline corresponds to a catalytic efficiency of at least 96 mmol/g/h.
The proposed approach applies to NM-HEAs containing up to five different metals.
The contemplated NM-HEA elements include Pt, Pd, Au, Ag, and Cu.
Each metal in the contemplated NM-HEA compositions has a concentration ranging from 10% to 30%.
The choice of exchange-correlation functional may affect the accuracy of DFT-predicted structures.
The treatment of dispersion forces may affect the accuracy of predicted structures and catalytic efficiency.
